Only somatic modifications with the person's informed consent are allowed; automated genetic editing is prohibited. Voluntary enhancement requires additional monitoring and reliable basic medical care.
Personal identity and bodily ownership continue uninterrupted; bodily ownership already vested in a person cannot be revoked afterward.

All residents with independent consciousness count toward population and provisioning needs as usual; those with equal civil rights also have representative seats. Civil rights already granted cannot be revoked afterward.

Commission mixed teams and clinical relief staffing

Costs 48 knowledge, 24 food, and 8 tools; 4 teachers on duty complete the handover in 180 seconds. People receiving clinical care take leave to recover; mechanical maintenance, synthetic manufacturing, and public administration all draw on registered residents, so no extra labor is created.
Commission clinical production and guaranteed supplies

Costs 12 parts, 40 knowledge, and 40 food; each period, spare medical staff at the follow-up station use 2 cultures, 8 food, 0.5 tools, and 8 power to produce 8 doses of medicine. Convoy runs prioritize maintaining four periods of food, medicine, and repair reserves; any surplus can be exported. No stock is created from nothing.
Commission clinical expansion and surplus medicine production

Costs 24 parts, 60 knowledge, and 12 tools; the construction limit for follow-up stations increases from 2 to 4. Stations still require separate materials to build, and each has 8 medical staff positions. When supplying others, medicine production quotas increase; local living reserves are protected first, and surplus medicine is then sent to the public warehouse on the same convoy.

Costs 4 knowledge; expenses already paid are not refunded, and goods already in transit still arrive as usual. Pausing the commission does not erase registered residents or remove existing rights and obligations.
